transcript: Do you ever love a show so much you're actually nervous about seeing it? That's how I felt about this production of next to normal, even though I had already seen it. When I saw it back in September at the Donmar Theatre, I was obsessed with it. It was my favourite show of 2023. I was a wreck. I love the performances. It felt so intimate and I was just worried I wouldn't have the same feeling. I shouldn't have been worried, though, because this production is next to perfect, and I'm so happy I came to see it a second time. The performances are devastating and nuanced, especially Casey Levy, who is just unreal as Diana. Jack Wolf literally plays Gabe as, like, this demon who is haunting his mother, and it's so good. Every time I see next to normal, different things stick out to me. And in this production especially, I love that they set the entire thing in a family kitchen. But I don't know about you, but the kitchen was the center of my home growing up. That was the spot where my family gathered. It was the heart of our home. And to watch Diana's heartbreak over and over again in this kitchen just destroyed me and many. Spoiler alert. When they turn the kitchen counter into the hospital bed where Diana is getting her electroshock therapy, it is like just gutting. My only complaint at all is that because the stage is So high at this theater, if you're in the stalls, you miss this one moment that was so powerful. And the audience reaction to that was one of my favorite moments of the Donmar production. And we just completely missed it. I love this musical so much. I love this music so much, and I'm so happy I got to see it one more time, and I really hope it comes to New York. Truly next to normal hits just as hard in 2,024 as it did in 2009.
classificationReason: Creator describes seeing production at Donmar Theatre, calls it favorite of 2023, gives detailed performance opinions, but show not on provided list
